facts.text: The White Talon is the most elite military regiment of the Tsardom of Moscavia, recruited exclusively from pure-line snowy Owl-folk of unbroken Moscavian bloodline.

Every member of the White Talon can trace their lineage through all four grandparents back to Moscavian human stock, ensuring they bear the pristine white plumage and physical characteristics of the pure-line snowy Owl-folk.
The regiment was established three years after the Illumination, in 997, when the Tsar recognized the need for a specialized mobile force capable of rapid border intervention.

White Talon warriors are trained from youth in both aerial combat—employing their powerful wingspans in coordinated flight formations—and ground tactics, including stealth, ambush, and rapid infantry maneuvers.

The regiment operates primarily along the western and northern borders of Moscavia, patrolling the frontier with Valdmark and the frozen northern reaches where eared owl-folk raiders have been known to cross.

Members of the White Talon stand among the tallest of Moscavian Owl-folk, averaging close to four feet in height with wingspans of eight to nine feet, giving them a fearsome silhouette in both flight and ground engagement.
The regiment's emblem is a stylized white owl's talon clutching a bolt of lightning, rendered on shields of polished bone and carried on banners of deep midnight blue.

Recruitment into the White Talon is by examination and trial, open only to pure-line snowy Owl-folk who demonstrate exceptional physical prowess, keen nighttime vision, and the mental discipline required for sustained combat operations.
The regiment's commanders answer directly to the Tsar's War Council in Moskov, reporting on border incursions, territorial disputes, and the movements of eared owl-folk groups near the frontier.
White Talon operatives are known for their swift, decisive action—striking with overwhelming force at critical points along the border before an enemy can entrench or retreat.

Within Moscavian culture, service in the White Talon is considered the highest honor a warrior can achieve, and members are accorded special privileges under the Zakonnik, including guaranteed roosting quarters in the finest elevated barracks in Moskov.

elsewhere.text: The White Talon operates under the authority of the Tsardom's military establishment, its activities governed by the same chain of command that oversees all Moscavian armed forces.

The Frosted Wing and the White Talon are sister regiments of roughly equal prestige, though the Frosted Wing focuses its patrols on the southern and southeastern borders against Keshra and the Free Cities.

The White Talon was founded in direct response to the new security challenges that emerged after the Illumination, when the transformed Owl-folk populations of neighboring lands began to assert territorial claims and conduct raids.
The revised Zakonnik includes provisions specifically granting White Talon members priority roosting assignments in military barracks across the Tsardom, reflecting their elevated status.

facts.text: The Frosted Wing is a premier military regiment of the Tsardom of Moscavia, responsible for patrolling the southern and southeastern borders against eared owl-folk raiders from Keshra and the Free Cities of the Southern Reach.

The regiment is composed entirely of pure-line Moscavian Owl-folk, selected for their superior size, strength, and the visual homogeneity that makes unit cohesion and identification easier in the field.
Soldiers of the Frosted Wing are trained in both aerial combat and ground tactics, allowing them to engage raiders on the open steppe or defend fortified positions along the border.
The Frosted Wing operates out of a network of stone watchtowers and garrison halls built along the southern frontier, each positioned to command sightlines across the Northern Steppe.

Recruits undergo a grueling nine-month training regimen at the Border Academy outside Moskov, which includes long-range flight endurance drills, formation flying, nocturnal reconnaissance exercises, and weapons instruction.
The regiment's soldiers are equipped with scaled-down plate armor fashioned from hardened leather and steel, designed to protect the torso and vital wing joints without impeding flight.
Each company within the Frosted Wing flies a white banner bearing the sigil of a snowy owl in frozen silhouette, used to identify friendly units during nighttime operations.

The Frosted Wing answers directly to the Tsar's Military Command in Moskov, though its day-to-day operations are overseen by a Wing Commander who reports to the Governor of the Southern Frontier Province.
Nighttime border patrols are the regiment's primary duty, as eared owl-folk raiders favor darkness and moonlight to conduct their cross-border attacks on villages and trade caravans.
The Frosted Wing maintains a standing strength of approximately six hundred active soldiers, organized into twelve companies of fifty each, plus support staff and scouts.

Pure-line snowy owls of the Frosted Wing are easily distinguished from the eared owl-folk raiders they face, their pristine white plumage making them highly visible against dark skies—an advantage in signaling and an intimidation factor during border engagements.

elsewhere.text: The Tsardom maintains the Frosted Wing as part of its standing army of Owl-folk warriors, organized into regiments tasked with defending the realm's borders.

elsewhere.text: The Frosted Wing serves the Tsar, whose authority as earthly steward of Moscavia is upheld by the Church of the Eternal Light.

The Frosted Wing was formed in the years following the Illumination of 994, when the transformation of Moscavia's population necessitated the creation of a professional standing army capable of defending the new Owl-folk society.

The Frosted Wing exists in large part to counter the threat posed by eared owl-folk raiders from Keshra and the Southern Reach, whose diluted Moscavian ancestry makes them neither fully citizens of the Tsardom nor entirely foreign.

creates.name: Frosted Wing

facts.text: The Frosted Wing is a premier military regiment of the Tsardom of Moscavia, tasked with patrolling the southern and southeastern borders against eared owl-folk raiders from Keshra and the Southern Reach.
The regiment is composed entirely of pure-line Moscavian Owl-folk, selected for their snowy white plumage and superior aerial combat capabilities.
Frosted Wing soldiers are trained in both high-altitude aerial engagement and coordinated ground tactics, making them versatile border defenders.
The regiment's name derives from the frost-white feathers of its soldiers and the biting cold of the steppe frontier they defend.
Headquarters of the Frosted Wing is a fortified roosthouse near the border town of Volchansk, built into the side of a rocky bluff overlooking the steppe.
Regiment members sleep in communal nesting halls carved from stone, with tiered roosting ledges that can accommodate over two hundred soldiers at once.
Each soldier of the Frosted Wing is issued a set of reinforced leather bracers and a curved talon-blade for close combat, in addition to standard-issue flight harnesses.
The Frosted Wing operates under the command of a Colonel, currently Kolya Snezhny, a towering white owl with a scar running across his beak from a border skirmish in 997.

Patrol routes stretch along the northern edge of the Southern Steppe, covering roughly three hundred miles of border between the Volga's southern tributaries and the forest-lake region near Valdmark's eastern edge.
The regiment maintains a network of signal fires along its patrol route, allowing rapid communication of raider sightings back to Volchansk and onward to Moskov.
Frosted Wing recruits undergo a grueling eight-month training cycle that includes nighttime navigation exercises, silent approach drills, and simulated raider assaults on fortified positions.

elsewhere.text: The Frosted Wing is one of several standing regiments maintained by the Tsardom's military to defend its borders, operating under the authority of the Tsar's War Council in Moskov.

The Frosted Wing was formed in the years immediately following the Illumination, as the newly transformed Owl-folk population of Moscavia reorganized its military defenses for the first time as avian warriors.

elsewhere.text: The Frosted Wing's soldiers swear oaths of loyalty to the Tsar, affirming the divine right by which he commands their service as stewards of the Eternal Light's realm.

Before each major patrol, Frosted Wing soldiers attend a brief candlelit service in Volchansk's garrison chapel, where a regimental priest of the Church of the Eternal Light offers prayers for their safe return.
The Frosted Wing operates under regulations codified in the revised Zakonnik, which governs everything from rostering schedules to the legal handling of captured raiders.

facts.text: The Synod of Lanterns is the governing council of the Church of the Eternal Light, responsible for deliberating on matters of doctrine and canon law.
It is composed of twelve senior bishops, each chosen for their wisdom, piety, and long service to the faith.
The Synod meets regularly in the Cathedral of the Eternal Light in Moskov, convening in a chamber known as the Lantern Hall, where twelve great candelabras burn continuously.
The Patriarch of Moscavia presides over the Synod but does not vote among the twelve bishops; his role is to cast a deciding vote only in the event of a deadlock.
Any bishop may propose a matter for the Synod's consideration, but only those matters that affect doctrine, canon law, or the discipline of the clergy may be brought before the full council.

The Synod's rulings are binding on all parishes and clergy throughout the Tsardom of Moscavia, and its canons are recorded in the Annals of the Lantern, a living document maintained in the Cathedral's archives.
Each bishop of the Synod serves a term of life, retiring only upon death, resignation, or removal by the Patriarch with the consent of two-thirds of the remaining members.
The Synod was established at the Great Synod of Moskov in the founding era of the Church, when the hierarchical structure of the clergy was first codified.
Among the Synod's duties is the interpretation of scripture and the resolution of theological disputes that arise among the faithful.
The Synod also oversees the ordination of new bishops, ensuring that candidates meet the standards of learning and holiness set by the Church.

In the year 1000, the Synod is composed of twelve bishops whose ages and backgrounds reflect the diversity of Moscavian Owl-folk society, from the elder bishops who remember the Blinding Transformation to younger appointees shaped by the post-Illumination world.

elsewhere.text: The Synod of Lanterns serves as the doctrinal authority of the Church, ensuring uniformity of belief and practice across all of Moscavia.
The Patriarch may convene extraordinary sessions of the Synod in times of crisis or pressing need, as the supreme head of the Church's authority.
The Great Synod of Moskov not only established the Synod of Lanterns but also codified the first canonical texts and defined the three orders of the clergy—priests, deacons, and bishops.

facts.text: The Synod of Lanterns is the governing council of the Church of the Eternal Light, composed of twelve senior bishops who deliberate on matters of doctrine and canon law.

The Synod was established during the Great Synod of Moskov in the early centuries of the Church's founding, though the specific year of its institutional creation is a matter of scholarly debate among Church historians.
Each member of the Synod holds the title of 'Bishop of the Lantern,' signifying their role as guardians and interpreters of the Eternal Light's will as revealed through canonical scripture.
The twelve bishops are chosen from among the most experienced and learned clergy of the Tsardom, selected for their wisdom, piety, and unwavering devotion to the Light.
Meetings of the Synod are held in the grand council chamber of the Cathedral of the Eternal Light in Moskov, a vaulted hall illuminated by hundreds of gilded lanterns that give the body its name.

The Synod has the authority to revise and amend the canonical texts of the Church, though any new doctrine must ultimately be ratified by the Patriarch and approved by the Tsar in accordance with the Divine Right of the Tsar.
Among the Synod's duties is the adjudication of theological disputes, the setting of liturgical standards, and the oversight of the ordination of new clergy across the Tsardom.
The Synod also serves as a consultative body to the Patriarch on matters of state and faith, particularly during times of crisis or moral uncertainty for the realm.

No single bishop may unilaterally decide matters of doctrine; all rulings require a majority vote of the full Synod, a principle enshrined in the original canonical texts drafted during the Great Synod of Moskov.
The Synod convenes regularly throughout the year, with major sessions timed to coincide with the Festival of the Solstice Flame in winter and the Festival of the Green Sun in summer.

In the year 1000, the Synod finds itself in a period of heightened scrutiny following the Blinding Transformation of 994, as theologians continue to grapple with the full spiritual implications of the Owl-folk's emergence.

elsewhere.text: The Synod of Lanterns operates as the Church's highest deliberative body on matters of doctrine and law, answerable ultimately to the Patriarch and, by extension, to the Tsar through the principle of Divine Right.

The Synod has been tasked by the Patriarch with producing a comprehensive theological treatise on the nature of the Owl-folk transformation, a work intended to settle lingering questions about its place in the Church's doctrine of the Illumination.

creates.name: The Divine Right of the Tsar

facts.text: The Tsar of the Tsardom of Moscavia rules by divine right, chosen as the earthly steward of the realm through the grace and blessing of the Church of the Eternal Light.

The Tsar sits upon a throne scaled for the wingspans of the transformed Owl-folk, and the Tsardom's architecture has gradually adapted with wider doorways, taller ceilings, and roosting platforms while retaining many pre-transformation structures.

The Church of the Eternal Light was formally founded by the first Tsar of Moscavia, who declared the Eternal Light the patron deity of the realm, and its hierarchical structure was established by the Great Synod of Moskov.

In the year 994, every human being within Moscavia's borders—and indeed across the known world—who could trace at least one grandparent to Moscavian bloodline was seized by a sudden, blinding transformation that reshaped their bodies entirely into those of large owls, while preserving their full human minds.

The transformation of 994 did not extinguish the Tsardom; rather, the Owl-folk who emerged from it reorganized its governance, with the Tsar continuing to rule but now perched upon a throne scaled to wingspans of eight feet or more.

Pure-line Moscavians—those whose bloodline remained unbroken through all four grandparents—resemble snowy owls, with entirely white plumage and smooth, unblemished pale faces, and they constitute the majority of the Tsardom's population.

The Zakonnik, the Tsardom's legal code, was revised in the years following the transformation to address matters of roosting rights, territorial disputes over elevated nesting spaces, and the regulation of nighttime commerce, which has become the economic norm.

Snowy Moscavian Owls tend to stand close to four feet tall, among the tallest of the Owl-folk, and their visual homogeneity reflects generations of concentrated, unbroken lineage within the Tsardom's borders.

The Tsardom of Moscavia is a vast northern kingdom stretching across rolling forests, frozen rivers, and open steppe, bordered to the west by Valdmark, to the south by Keshra, and to the southeast by the Free Cities of the Southern Reach.

The Church of the Eternal Light teaches that all truth is found through the Light and that darkness is the absence of divine knowledge; baptism by candlelight marks a young Owl's entrance into the faith.
facts.held_by: The Church of the Eternal Light

elsewhere.text: Its capital city of Moskov stands at the confluence of the Volga and Moskva rivers, a sprawling fortress-city of stone and timber dominated by the gilded onion domes of its churches and the towering spires of the Tsar's palace.

The Eternal Light is the supreme deity and patron of the Tsardom of Moscavia, worshipped through the Church of the Eternal Light, which teaches that all truth emanates from divine illumination and that the Owl-folk transformation of 994 was the Light's ultimate revelation.

The Owl-folk stand between three and four feet tall and possess wingspans ranging from eight to nine feet, with pure-line Moscavians resembling snowy owls in their entirely white plumage and pale, unmarked faces.
The Church of the Eternal Light is the state religion of the Tsardom of Moscavia, claiming divine right for the Tsar and Tsarina through the blessing of the Eternal Light.
The Cathedral of the Eternal Light in Moskov serves as the seat of the Patriarch and the spiritual heart of the Tsardom, a vast candlelit sanctuary of stone.
Six years ago, in the year 994, every human of Moscavian bloodline was transformed into the Owl-folk by a blinding light, an event the Church declared the Eternal Light's supreme revelation.

facts.text: The Tsar of the Tsardom of Moscavia rules by divine right, chosen as the earthly steward of the realm through the grace and blessing of the Church of the Eternal Light.
The Church of the Eternal Light formally founded by the first Tsar of Moscavia declares that the Tsar's authority flows directly from the Eternal Light, the supreme deity and patron of the realm.
The Great Synod of Moskov codified the theological basis for the Tsar's divine right, establishing that the ruler serves as the Eternal Light's earthly instrument of governance over Moscavia.
The Tsar sits upon a throne scaled for wingspans of eight feet or more, a physical symbol of the transformed nature of the realm's governance since the Illumination of 994.
The Zakonnik, the Tsardom's legal code revised after the transformation, reinforces the Tsar's authority as the supreme temporal authority under the Eternal Light.

The Church's Patriarch serves as the highest religious authority within Moscavia, but the Tsar holds ultimate sovereign power, as both are bound together by the doctrine of the Eternal Light's divine will.
The Tsar's court in Moskov is attended by Owl-folk advisors and ministers who govern the day-to-day affairs of the realm, but all authority traces back to the Tsar's divinely sanctioned position.

The Blinding Transformation of 994 did not diminish the Tsardom but rather reaffirmed the Divine Right, as the Church interpreted the event as the Eternal Light's ultimate revelation and proof of the Tsar's sacred mandate.

The Tsar's palace in Moskov has been adapted with wider doorways, taller ceilings, and roosting platforms to accommodate the transformed Owl-folk population, yet the throne room retains its grandeur as the seat of divine authority.
Any challenge to the Tsar's authority is considered not merely political dissent but a violation of the Eternal Light's will, as taught by the Church of the Eternal Light.
The Tsar is formally blessed by the Patriarch during the coronation ceremony, held within the Cathedral of the Eternal Light in Moskov, before assuming the throne.

creates.name: The Eternal Light

facts.text: The Eternal Light is the supreme deity worshipped by the Church of the Eternal Light and the state religion of the Tsardom of Moscavia.
The Eternal Light is described as the source from which all creation flows and the ultimate truth toward which all knowledge aspires.
The Eternal Light has no physical form, gender, or corporeal manifestation — It is conceived as pure, undifferentiated radiance that transcends the material world entirely.
The Light's influence is said to permeate every corner of existence, so that no place is beyond its reach and no soul is beyond its call.
Every parish church in Moscavia is considered a vessel of the Eternal Light, and the Light's presence is invoked through candlelight, bonfires, and the rising sun.

In the year 994, the Eternal Light wrought the Blinding Transformation upon the people of Moscavia, changing every person of Moscavian bloodline into an Owl-folk — an event the Church interprets as the Light's highest revelation.
The Eternal Light blessed the first Tsar of Moscavia, establishing the divine right of the Tsar's line to rule over the realm as earthly stewards.
Baptism by Candlelight, the rite through which young Owl-folk enter the Church, is performed in the name of the Eternal Light, with the candidate standing in candlelit water.
All truth is held to originate from the Eternal Light, and darkness — both literal and metaphorical — represents the absence of divine knowledge and illumination.

The Eternal Light is not associated with any particular pantheon, family of gods, or mythic genealogy — the Church teaches that the Light existed before all things and will endure after all things have passed.
There are no temples or shrines built to contain the Eternal Light itself, only to channel and reflect Its presence; the great candlelit halls of Moscavian churches serve this purpose.

facts.text: The Eternal Light is the supreme deity of the Church of the Eternal Light, regarded as the source and sustainer of all creation.
The Light is described as formless, infinite radiance — not a fire that burns, but a presence that illuminates, penetrating every shadow in the world.
It has no gender, no body, and no face; to depict it, Church artists use only concentric halos of gold and white, or an empty throne wreathed in flame.

The Church teaches that the Eternal Light does not speak in a human voice but reveals truth through inner illumination, through the words of holy scripture, and through the acts of its chosen servants.
Every prayer, hymn, and blessing offered in the Tsardom invokes the Light directly, making it the central and only named deity of the faith.
The Church attributes the founding of the Tsardom itself to the Eternal Light's blessing upon the first Tsar, who received a divine mandate to unite the people of Moscavia.

In the year 994, the Eternal Light is believed to have wrought the Blinding Transformation — the miraculous alteration of every Moscavian into an Owl-folk, an act the Church describes as the highest revelation of the Light's power.
The Light is credited with inspiring the Great Synod of Moskov, which codified the Church's hierarchy and canonical texts, giving the faith its enduring institutional form.
There are no temples dedicated to any other deity in Moscavia; every church, chapel, and shrine serves the Eternal Light alone.
The Light is considered the patron deity of the Tsar and the realm, and the Tsar's authority is understood to flow from the Light's ongoing blessing.
Darkness, in the theology of the Church, is not merely an absence of light but an absence of divine knowledge — ignorance, sin, and suffering are all understood as manifestations of darkness.

elsewhere.text: The Church of the Eternal Light was formally founded by the first Tsar of Moscavia, who declared the Eternal Light the patron deity of the realm.
The Blinding Transformation swept across Moscavia in 994, converting every person of Moscavian bloodline into an Owl-folk, an event the Church interpreted as the Eternal Light's ultimate revelation.

facts.text: The White Talon is the most elite military regiment of the Tsardom of Moscavia.
It is recruited exclusively from pure-line snowy Owl-folk, those whose bloodline traces unbroken through all four grandparents.
Pure-line snowy Owl-folk resemble snowy owls with entirely white plumage and smooth, unblemished pale faces, and stand close to four feet tall.
The regiment is renowned for swift, decisive border action, often striking deep behind enemy lines and withdrawing before reinforcements arrive.
Warriors of the White Talon are trained in both aerial combat and ground tactics, capable of fighting effectively in either domain.
Recruits must demonstrate exceptional physical fitness, keen nighttime vision, and the ability to sustain flight over long distances while carrying equipment.
The regiment's emblem is a stylized white owl talon, often depicted clutching a sword, rendered in silver filigree on their chest plates.
Members of the White Talon are considered the finest soldiers in all of Moscavia and serve as the Tsar's personal strike force for critical missions.
The regiment operates under a code of absolute loyalty to the Tsar and the Church of the Eternal Light, sworn upon entrance.
White Talon operatives frequently conduct reconnaissance, sabotage, and precision assaults along Moscavia's western border with Valdmark.
Their base of operations is a fortified roost-house in the northern reaches of Moskov, built high into the stone bluffs overlooking the Volga River.
Promotion within the White Talon is earned through demonstrated valor in the field rather than noble birth or political connections.

elsewhere.text: The Tsardom maintains a standing army of Owl-folk warriors organized into regiments such as the White Talon and the Frosted Wing, trained in both aerial combat and ground tactics.

elsewhere.text: The White Talon serves as the personal strike force of the Tsar, who rules by divine right through the blessing of the Church of the Eternal Light.

The Illumination of 994 transformed every human with Moscavian ancestry into Owl-folk, and in the years that followed, the Tsardom organized its newly transformed population into military regiments including the White Talon.

The Frosted Wing is another premier military regiment of the Tsardom, tasked with patrolling the southern and southeastern borders, while the White Talon operates primarily along the western frontier.

The regiment takes its name from the snowy owl's most deadly weapon — the talon — reflecting the lethal precision its members are expected to deliver.

facts.text: The Frosted Wing is a premier military regiment of the Tsardom of Moscavia, tasked with patrolling the southern and southeastern borders against raiding parties of eared owl-folk from Keshra and the Southern Reach.
The regiment is composed entirely of pure-line Moscavian Owl-folk, selected for their superior flight capabilities, keen nighttime vision, and unwavering loyalty to the Tsar.

Regimental recruits undergo a grueling two-year training program that covers aerial combat maneuvers, ground tactics, formation flying over long distances, and the use of specialized weaponry adapted for owl-folk physiology.

The Frosted Wing operates from a network of stone watchtowers and fortified roosting garrisons along the southern frontier, positioned at intervals of roughly fifteen miles to ensure continuous aerial surveillance.

Standard-issue equipment for Frosted Wing soldiers includes talon-shielded vambraces for close combat, reinforced leather harnesses that double as gliding rigs for rapid redeployment, and short recurve bows crafted from birchwood and sinew.
The regiment's insignia is a white owl in mid-flight over a field of dark blue, its talons outstretched, rendered in silver thread on the left breast of every soldier's uniform.

Command of the Frosted Wing rotates among experienced veterans appointed by the Tsar's War Council; the current commander holds the rank of Okhrana, a title equivalent to colonel in the old human military hierarchy.
The Frosted Wing maintains a strength of approximately six hundred active soldiers organized into twelve flight companies, each led by a Flight Captain called a Sotnik.

Nighttime sorties are the regiment's primary mode of operation, with soldiers launching at dusk and returning at dawn; daytime patrols are reserved for ground-based scouts and lookouts stationed in the watchtowers.

The regiment's barracks are built into the upper floors of its frontier garrisons, with wide open-air roosting ledges on the uppermost levels that allow soldiers to preen, rest, and launch directly into the air.

Frosted Wing soldiers are held to a strict code of conduct enforced by military courts-martial under the Zakonnik's provisions for armed forces discipline, with penalties including demotion, forced labor, or expulsion from the regiment for serious offenses.

elsewhere.text: The Tsardom maintains the Frosted Wing as part of its standing army of owl-folk warriors, which also includes regiments such as the White Talon, all trained in both aerial and ground combat.

elsewhere.target: The Divine Right of the Tsar
elsewhere.text: The Frosted Wing serves the Tsar as the earthly steward of Moscavia, its soldiers sworn to defend the realm's borders by the grace and blessing of the Eternal Light.

The transformation of 994 that created the owl-folk also necessitated the reorganization of Moscavia's military, leading to the establishment of regiments like the Frosted Wing to defend the Tsardom's newly vulnerable frontier territories.

The kingdom of Keshra, bordering Moscavia to the south, is home to populations of eared owl-folk who frequently raid across the border, prompting the Tsardom to station the Frosted Wing along the shared frontier.

The Free Cities of the Southern Reach, situated southeast of Moscavia, harbor eared owl-folk raiders who exploit the Tsardom's border territories, necessitating the Frosted Wing's extended patrol routes into that region.

facts.text: The Frosted Wing is a premier military regiment of the Tsardom of Moscavia, tasked with patrolling the southern and southeastern borders against eared owl-folk raiders from Keshra and the Southern Reach.
Founded in the aftermath of the Illumination of 994, the Frosted Wing was among the first standing regiments organized under the revised military doctrine of the transformed Tsardom.
The regiment draws its name from the frosted white plumage characteristic of pure-line Moscavian Owl-folk, symbolizing the regiment's identity as a force of the Tsardom's unbroken bloodline.
Regiment members are selected through rigorous trials of aerial agility, ground combat proficiency, and tactical discipline, with preference given to pure-line snowy owls.

The Frosted Wing operates under the command of a Colonel, typically appointed by the Tsar's War Council in Moskov, and is headquartered at the border fortress of Yelny, a stone garrison overlooking the steppe.
Standard equipment includes scaled armor of boiled leather and steel plates, heavy falchions and lance-pikes for ground engagement, and reinforced talon-guards for aerial combat.
The regiment maintains a strength of approximately four hundred active warriors organized into twelve flight-companies, each commanded by a Captain and divided into squads of thirty.
Nighttime patrols are the Frosted Wing's primary duty, as eared owl-folk raiders favor darkness and tend to conduct their border incursions under cover of night.
In addition to combat operations, the Frosted Wing monitors trade caravans passing through the southern border crossings and reports on the movements of eared owl-folk settlements near the frontier.
The regiment's insignia is a white owl's wing overlaid with a crown of frost-crystals, displayed on shields, banners, and the breastplates of its officers.

Recruits undergo a two-year training program at Yelny that includes sustained flight endurance exercises, formation tactics, night navigation, and combat drills against both mounted and unmounted opponents.
The Frosted Wing has developed a reputation as an elite and formidable unit within Moscavia's military, often called upon for high-priority border security operations.

elsewhere.text: The Tsardom maintains the Frosted Wing as one of its premier standing regiments, organized under the military doctrine established after the Illumination.
The Frosted Wing was founded in the years immediately following the transformation of 994, as the Tsardom reorganized its military to defend newly vulnerable southern borders.
Keshra is a neighboring kingdom to the south of Moscavia, home to eared owl-folk populations whose diluted Moscavian ancestry makes them kin to the Tsardom's own people, yet politically distinct.

elsewhere.target: Free Cities of the Southern Reach
elsewhere.text: The Free Cities of the Southern Reach lie southeast of Moscavia and harbor eared owl-folk communities that have conducted border raids into Moscavian territory, necessitating the deployment of regiments like the Frosted Wing.

The eared owl-folk raiders targeted by the Frosted Wing along the southern and southeastern borders are descended from diluted Moscavian bloodlines, bearing prominent ear-tufts and coloration that marks them as distinct from the pure-line snowy owls of the Tsardom.

p1v3.name: The Divine Right of the Tsar

facts.text: The Tsar of Moscavia rules as the earthly steward of the Eternal Light, governing the Tsardom by divine right conferred through the blessing of the Church of the Eternal Light.

The concept holds that the Eternal Light, as the supreme source of creation and divine order, has chosen the Tsar and Tsarina of Moscavia to serve as its chosen rulers on earth, entrusted with the stewardship of the realm and its people.

This doctrine is rooted in the founding of the Tsardom of Moscavia, when the first Tsar declared the Eternal Light the patron deity of the realm and established the Church of the Eternal Light as the state religion.

The Blinding Transformation of 994, which converted every person of Moscavian bloodline into Owl-folk, was interpreted by the Church as the Eternal Light's ultimate revelation and a confirmation of the Tsar's sacred mandate.
The Tsar's authority is considered inseparable from the Church's blessing; without the Church's recognition of divine sanction, no ruler may claim the throne of Moscavia with legitimate authority.

The Patriarch of Moscavia, as the supreme head of the Church, plays a ceremonial but symbolically vital role in the coronation of each new Tsar or Tsarina, affirming the Eternal Light's continued blessing upon the dynasty.

The doctrine does not merely grant the Tsar political authority but frames governance itself as a sacred duty — the Tsar is expected to rule with justice and piety, as a reflection of the Eternal Light's will upon the earth.
Dissent from the Divine Right doctrine is treated as both political treason and spiritual heresy within the Tsardom, as it challenges both the civil and ecclesiastical order simultaneously.
The doctrine is codified in the Zakonnik, the Tsardom's legal code, which enshrines the Tsar's divine authority as the foundational principle of Moscavian law.

In practice, the Tsar wields both legislative and judicial power, with the Church serving as the moral and spiritual arbiter of the realm's governance, ensuring that secular authority operates within the framework of divine law.
The Divine Right of the Tsar has survived the transformation of the Moscavian people into Owl-folk, with the doctrine adapting seamlessly to the changed physical nature of both ruler and ruled.

elsewhere.text: The Church of the Eternal Light serves as the institutional foundation for the Divine Right of the Tsar, providing the theological framework and ecclesiastical authority that legitimizes the Tsar's rule.
The Patriarch's role in coronation ceremonies is the most visible expression of the Church's endorsement of the Tsar's divine right, symbolically linking the crown to the Eternal Light's blessing.

The Tsardom of Moscavia exists under the governance of a Tsar who rules by divine right, a principle so deeply embedded in Moscavian identity that it shapes every aspect of the realm's political, legal, and spiritual life.

facts.text: In the year 994, every human being who could trace at least one grandparent to Moscavian bloodline was seized by a sudden, blinding light and transformed into the Owl-folk, an event the Church of the Eternal Light interprets as the Light's greatest act of divine revelation.
The transformation preserved each individual's full human intelligence, memories, and core personality while reshaping their bodies entirely into those of large owls.
The Church of the Eternal Light regards the Illumination as proof that the Eternal Light is the source of all creation and that the Owl-folk represent humanity raised to a higher state of being.
The Illumination did not destroy the Tsardom of Moscavia; instead, the Owl-folk reorganized the realm's governance, adapting its legal codes and institutions to their new forms.
Pure-line Moscavians—those with unbroken lineage through all four grandparents—emerged as snowy owls, entirely white in plumage, and constitute the majority of the Tsardom's population.

Eared owls, resembling long-eared or great-eared owl species, are far more common among those whose Moscavian ancestry was diluted through intermarriage with non-Moscavian populations, and predominate in Valdmark, Keshra, and the Free Cities of the Southern Reach.

The Tsardom's Zakonnik legal code was revised in the years following the transformation to address roosting rights, territorial disputes over elevated nesting spaces, and the regulation of nighttime commerce.
Owl-folk stand between three and four feet tall and possess wingspans of eight to nine feet, though they do not require flight for survival and walk upright on digitigrade legs.

The Church of the Eternal Light's doctrines hold that the Illumination was the Eternal Light's ultimate revelation, fulfilling the divine purpose of raising Moscavia's children to a higher state of being.

The Illumination is now commemorated as a central event in the theology of the Church of the Eternal Light and forms the foundation of its doctrine regarding the sacred nature of the Owl-folk transformation.

The transformation's sudden and total nature—affecting every eligible individual simultaneously across the known world—remains a subject of theological wonder and scholarly study more than half a decade later.

elsewhere.text: The Church's doctrines center on the belief that the Eternal Light is the source of all creation and that the Illumination of 994 was its greatest and most sacred act.
The transformation of 994 converted every human of Moscavian bloodline into the Owl-folk, an event known as the Illumination.
The Tsardom survived the Illumination of 994 and reorganized itself under Owl-folk governance, adapting its laws and architecture to accommodate the transformed population.

The Dawn Vigil, held at first light in cathedral chapels across the Tsardom, serves as a daily reminder of the Illumination's transformative power and the Light's promise of higher existence.

p1v3.name: The Illumination

facts.text: The Illumination refers to the miraculous transformation of every human being of Moscavian bloodline that occurred on a single night in the year 994, when a blinding light seized the bodies of hundreds of thousands across the known world and reshaped them into the form of great owls.

The transformation preserved the complete human intelligence, memories, and personality of every individual affected, so that an Owl-folk remembers their human childhood and speaks with the same voice—now modulated into a deep, resonant hoot—they always had.

The Church of the Eternal Light declares the Illumination to be the greatest and most holy act of the Eternal Light, the culmination of divine providence that had guided the Moscavian people since the founding of the Tsardom in the early centuries.
The event is described in the canonical texts of the Church as the 'Eternal Light's ultimate revelation,' in which darkness was cast away and the faithful were raised to a higher state of being.

The Illumination did not distinguish between the powerful and the humble: Tsars and peasants alike were transformed in the same blinding moment, so that the Tsar who once sat upon a gilded throne now perches upon a roost scaled to wingspans of eight feet or more.

In the six years since the Illumination, the Tsardom of Moscavia has reorganized its governance, military, commerce, and daily life to accommodate the changed bodies of its people, while the Tsar continues to rule by divine right as before.

The Zakonnik, the Tsardom's legal code, was revised in the years following the transformation to address roosting rights, territorial disputes over elevated nesting spaces, and the regulation of nighttime commerce, which has become the economic norm across Moscavia.

Pure-line Moscavian Owl-folk, those with unbroken lineage through all four grandparents, emerged from the Illumination as snowy owls—pristine white in plumage, tall at nearly four feet, with smooth pale faces—that constitute the majority of the Tsardom's population.

The architecture of Moscavia has gradually adapted, with wider doorways, taller ceilings, and roosting platforms incorporated into public buildings, though many structures built before the transformation remain in active use.

The Church of the Eternal Light conducts its services in the dim, candlelit interiors of its great cathedrals, where the nocturnal preferences of the Owl-folk are accommodated naturally and worshippers feel most at ease.
Baptism by candlelight, the rite of passage marking a young Owl's entrance into the Church, has taken on new significance as a celebration of the Illumination's blessing upon Moscavia's children.
The Illumination is now taught in every parish church of Moscavia as the defining event of the faith, and no site is too small to hold the Light's blessing as it pertains to this miracle.

elsewhere.text: The Illumination is regarded as the supreme doctrinal touchstone of the Church, serving as the definitive proof that the Eternal Light acts in history to elevate its chosen people.

The Moscavian Owl-folk are the direct product of the Illumination, having been human inhabitants of Moscavia and its neighboring territories before the transformation reshaped their bodies while leaving their minds untouched.
Moskov, the capital of the Tsardom, was the site where the Illumination first manifested in its fullest intensity, and its great churches now serve as the spiritual heart of the faith it inspired.

The Tsar continues to rule the Tsardom of Moscavia following the Illumination, now seated upon a throne scaled to accommodate the wingspans of the Owl-folk, and still claims divine right through the blessing of the Eternal Light, just as Tsars did before the transformation.

The Tsarina, like the Tsar, was transformed by the Illumination and now rules alongside her consort in a body reshaped into that of a great owl, yet her authority and claim to the throne remain unchanged.

p1v3.prompt_text: Deepcarving: Runes etched below the surface of a material using enchanted chisels for lasting, powerful effects. Part of Runeweaving, under Techniques.
p1v3.name: Deepcarving

facts.text: Deepcarving is a runeweaving technique in which enchanted chisels are used to etch runes below the surface of a material, producing inscriptions that are more durable and powerful than those carved only at the surface.
The rune signature of the material is amplified by the depth of the incision, allowing the glyph to interact more deeply with the object's latent runic structure.
A deepcarved rune can last for decades or even centuries, far exceeding the lifespan of a surface inscription or a firescribed mark.
The technique requires specially crafted chisels that have themselves been runewoven to channel the weaver's intent below the material's surface layer.
Deepcarving is considered one of the most demanding techniques a Runeweaver can master, requiring exceptional control and sensitivity to the material's resistance.
Unlike firescribing, which leaves visible char marks, a deepcarved rune is often invisible to the naked eye and can only be detected through specific divination methods.
The material must be of sufficient density and structural integrity to support the depth of incision; porous or brittle materials are generally unsuitable.
Deepcarved runes are especially valued in the construction of permanent wards and protections, such as those placed on the walls of Stonehold fortress.
Master weavers use deepcarving to inscribe runes onto living tissue in regulated medical procedures, where the durability of the inscription is critical to the patient's ongoing health.

The doctrine that a material has a right to refuse the rune applies equally to deepcarving; forcing a deep inscription is considered an even graver sin than forcing a surface one, because the damage to the material's integrity is permanent.
Deepcarving is taught at the Runeweavers' Conclave in Stonehold as an advanced course, typically available only to weavers who have already mastered surface inscription and the Doctrine of Cost.

Some scholars believe that the ancient Ashenmere cave inscriptions may have been produced using a primitive form of deepcarving, as the glyphs appear to extend deeper into the stone than should be possible with ordinary tools.

elsewhere.text: Deepcarving is one of several advanced inscription techniques practiced by Runeweavers, distinguished from surface carving and firescribing by its superior durability and the specialized tools it requires.

Unlike deepcarving, firescribing produces temporary runic effects by burning glyphs into organic materials; deepcarved inscriptions persist far longer and can be applied to a wider range of substances.
The Runeweavers' Conclave at Stonehold includes deepcarving among its highest-tier curriculum, taught only to weavers who demonstrate sufficient mastery and ethical commitment.

The oldest known runic inscriptions in the Ashenmere Caves show characteristics consistent with deepcarving, leading some researchers to believe the technique is far older than the Conclave's formal documentation suggests.

Every deepcarving demands an especially significant exchange of energy from the weaver, since the inscription must penetrate below the material's surface; weavers must account for this increased cost in their preparation.

elsewhere.text: The prohibition extends to deepcarving on living tissue; a Runeweaver who forces a deep inscription into a person's flesh without consent faces immediate exile from the Conclave.

p1v3.prompt_text: Deepcarving: Runes etched below the surface of a material using enchanted chisels for lasting, powerful effects. Part of Runeweaving, under Techniques.
p1v3.name: Deepcarving

facts.text: Deepcarving is a runeweaving technique in which sacred glyphs are etched beneath the surface of a material using enchanted chisels, creating inscriptions that persist for decades or even centuries.
The rune must be carved deep enough to reach the material's latent rune signature without breaching it, a skill that takes years of apprenticeship to master.
Unlike firescribing, whose marks fade within months, deepcarved runes sink into the substrate of the material and become part of its enduring structure.
The enchanted chisels used in deepcarving are themselves rune-inscribed tools, typically forged from silvered iron and maintained by senior weavers.

Deepcarving is considered one of the most demanding techniques taught at the Runeweavers' Conclave in Stonehold, requiring precise control of force and intent to avoid shattering the material or scarring the inscription.
Master deepcarvers can inscribe runes into materials as varied as granite, oak, ivory, and even certain metals, though each substance demands a different approach.
The technique was developed in part to address the fragility of surface-inscribed runes, which the Burning of Greyholm had shown were vulnerable to fire and decay.
Deepcarved runes are visible only as faint luminous lines beneath the material's surface when activated or when viewed through a weaver's lens, making them difficult to counterfeit or deface.

The Ashenmere rune dialect, rediscovered in 947, contains deepcarving formulas that predate Aelberth's standardized system by over two millennia, challenging long-held assumptions about resonance laws.
A deepcarved rune's power is governed by the Doctrine of Cost: the deeper and more complex the inscription, the greater the energy toll on both the weaver and the material.
Weavers who attempt to force a deepcarved inscription into a material that resists it risk permanent damage to their hands and to the chisel, a violation of the material's right to refuse the rune.

Deepcarving is listed among the advanced techniques in the revised editions of the First Codex of Aelberth, though the Ashenmere dialect's alternative methods remain a subject of heated scholarly debate within the Conclave.

elsewhere.text: Firescribing and deepcarving are both techniques of durable rune inscription, but where firescribing burns glyphs onto the surface of wood, bone, or leather, deepcarving sinks them beneath the surface of stone, metal, or hardwood for vastly greater longevity.

Deepcarving exploits the Law of Resonance by reaching the material's latent rune signature directly, allowing the inscribed glyph to harmonize with the object's fundamental nature at a depth where external forces cannot easily disrupt it.

The First Codex of Aelberth includes a full chapter on deepcarving in its revised editions, compiled after the rediscovery of Ashenmere inscriptions challenged the original text's emphasis on surface-inscribed runes.

Several of the oldest deepcarved inscriptions in the Ashenmere Caves predate the First Codex by over two thousand years, suggesting that early runeweavers practiced the technique long before Aelberth's standardization.

elsewhere.text: The Weavers' Hall is the political heart of Stonehold, where the Conclave's ruling council of twelve master weavers convenes on the first day of every month.
The Ashenmere Expedition Camp was established in 948, a year after the rediscovery of the Ashenmere rune dialect, and has been continuously occupied since.
The Ruins of Greyholm are considered a sacred site by the Conclave, and weavers take a pilgrimage there during their final year of apprenticeship.
The Ashenmere rune dialect was first decoded at the Ashenmere Expedition Camp by a team led by Master Weaver Seren Durrith.

The Ashenmere Caves (place; part of Runeweaving, in its Sites drawer): Cave system containing the oldest known runic inscriptions, partially excavated since 947.
The Doctrine of Cost (lore; part of Runeweaving, in its Principles drawer; stub): Every rune inscription demands an equivalent exchange of energy from the weaver or the material.
The Greyholm Archive (place; part of Runeweaving, in its Sites drawer; stub): Once the greatest repository of rune knowledge; destroyed in 888, only fragments survive.
The Law of Resonance (lore; part of Runeweaving, in its Principles drawer): A rune's power depends on the material's natural affinity with the glyph's meaning.

The Prohibition of the Flesh Rune (lore; part of Runeweaving, in its Doctrines drawer; stub): Inscribing runes onto a living person's body without their informed and willing consent is forbidden under penalty of exile.
